# Math Escape Lab
SymPy → Java

The Golden / Snub matrix is now wrapped in a local Python + NumPy + SymPy + Java runtime. The rule is intentionally weird: **SymPy cannot reach Java directly.** It has to derive an exact root, survive a NumPy independent check, print itself as Java source, compile with `javac`, and then convince the JVM that the original polynomial residual is tiny.

### JVM output

ESCAPED label=(1, δs) value=2.4142135623730950 residual=-3.3306690738754696e-16 coordinate_norm=2.6457513110645907 JAVA_GATE_ACCEPTED  Generated Java source

```
public final class EscapeKernelPellSilver {
    static double derivedValue() {
        return 1 + Math.sqrt(2);
    }

    static double polynomialResidual(double x) {
        double[] c = new double[]{ 1, -2, -1 };
        double y = 0.0;
        for (double a : c) y = y * x + a;
        return y;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        double value = derivedValue();
        double residual = polynomialResidual(value);
        double inv = 1.0 / value;
        double norm = Math.sqrt(1.0 + inv * inv + value * value);
        System.out.printf("ESCAPED\nlabel=(1, δs)\nvalue=%.17g\nresidual=%.17g\ncoordinate_norm=%.17g\n", value, residual, norm);
        if (!Double.isFinite(value) || Math.abs(residual) > 1e-10) {
            System.err.println("JAVA_GATE_REJECTED");
            System.exit(2);
        }
        System.out.println("JAVA_GATE_ACCEPTED");
    }
}
```
